KILLED 1

stopped by a stated criterion

#latch-pilot-killed KILLED LINKED as of 2026-11-11

The Latch pilot, a typed-operator admission gate against free chain-of-thought on multi-hop QA, was killed at its preregistered G3 gate: the gated arm scored 37.5% at full coverage against 80.6% for chain-of-thought.

Reported numbers
Numbers for latch-pilot-killed
MetricValuen / denominatorDatasetSyntheticSystemDate
accuracy at full coverage, Arm 0 (CoT) vs Arm 2 (gate)80.6% vs 37.5% (-43.1 pp)58/72 vs 27/722WikiMultihopQA validation, annotated-decomposable subset of a 100-question stratified samplenoqwen2.5:14b, v4 prompts2026-11-11
Arm 2 abstention / precision on admitted55.6% / 84.4%40/72 abstained; 27/32 admitted correctsamenosame2026-11-11
Arm 0 on the same 32 admitted questions90.6%29/32samenosame2026-11-11
Kill criterion
PREREG.md, G3: promote only if Arm 2 beats Arm 0 by >= 15 pp at full coverage with p < 0.05 (McNemar); kill if Arm 2 loses to Arm 0.
Does not show
Anything about gates that anchor to literal artifacts (fetched bytes, export rows). It tests a model translating a free-form question into a formal schema. Scoring was manual and not blinded; few-shot Example 5 was written from errors in the same 72 questions, which makes Arm 2's number optimistic; and PREREG section 5 treats abstentions as 'not answered, never wrong' while the headline scores them as wrong. The kill clause holds under either reading.
Sources disagree
The McNemar statistic on the 32 jointly answered questions (b=4, c=2) appears as chi2 = 0.167 in POSTMORTEM.md and the vault, and as chi2 = 0.67, p = 0.41 in paper.tex. Both come from the same cells; the site builder's reading is that one uses a continuity correction, which the author has not confirmed. Neither changes the kill.
Evidence
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : docs/POSTMORTEM.md tier 1 — committed version; the worktree has uncommitted edits to this file, not used here
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : PREREG.md tier 1 — G3 promote/kill criteria; unchanged since 37b8a9c
  • Latch @ study3-agent-gate cdcd512 : LOG.md tier 1 — G3 KILL entry, commit 4adbb01
Notes
Stage history from POSTMORTEM: G1 promoted (74/100 decomposable; re-annotation 72/100, kappa 0.949). G2 was killed under the strict gate (0% admit), the gate and prompts were redesigned, G2 was killed again on manual review (16 of 26 non-trivial admits structurally valid but semantically wrong), then promoted at about 50% correct formalization with v4 prompts. G3 then killed the pilot.

BUILT but not measured 9

Built entries with no qualifying measurement in the evidence. Full entries are in the ledger and on project pages.

  • #gin-bookkeeper The Bookkeeper is the single admission gate for GIN's graph state: it checks a confidence floor, endpoint existence, self-loops, anchor integrity, duplicates and DAG acyclicity, then stamps provenance on what it admits. Does not show: Any measurement of the Bookkeeper. The walk found code and tests, not an eval output for the gate itself. The checks are structural; they do not judge whether an admitted relation is true.
  • #gin-sear-decode-constraint GIN's SEAR layer constrains every generated token, at decode time, to continue a span that occurs verbatim in the retrieved corpus, using a custom llama-cpp-python logits processor. Does not show: That the constrained output is correct or fair to its source. Verbatim spans can still be selected or juxtaposed misleadingly. It also does not show behaviour on native Windows: the repo notes the generation path is only exercised under Linux/WSL.
  • #sear-demo-pipeline sear-demo is a corpus-grounded answer pipeline with a verification gate: the model writes freely, then each claim must be entailed by its cited chunk (NLI) and every name and number must appear in it, or the claim is dropped; an explicit failure state replaces guessing. Does not show: Decode-time constraint: this is SEAR's verify-after stage, not GIN's decode-time mask. Verified is not true: the gate enforces the corpus, not the world (see sear-poisoned-fork).
  • #sear-demo-results On its 27-probe main set, sear-demo refused all 9 probes that should be refused, but 5 of its 14 failure states were on probes that had a supportable answer. Does not show: A measurement. The README says every number is a smoke test, not a measurement (13 chunks, 27 + 6 + 5 probes). Retrieval is not tested: top_k 12 of 13 chunks means the generator sees almost the whole corpus.
  • #assay-library Assay is the claim-audit constraint layer extracted from Receipts into a standalone TypeScript library (v0.1.0): corpus plus subject in, a ledger or a reasoned refusal out. Does not show: Use outside Receipts' own field profile. An exact substring is not a fair reading of its source (README Limits). The local repo has no git remote, so publication cannot be confirmed here.
  • #receipts-pipeline Receipts is a TypeScript pipeline that reads a vendor's pages and independent sources (including SEC filings, NHTSA and IIHS), lets a model propose which claims contradict which, and discards any quote a deterministic gate cannot re-find in the fetched bytes. Does not show: That a verbatim quote is a fair reading of its source, or that a proposed relation is real (see receipts-relation-check). The submission itself is not evidenced in the repo.
  • #receipts-tesla-ledger The Tesla FSD ledger has no DIVERGENT or corroborated row; its strongest rows are two DISPUTED ones, such as Tesla's FSD page ('helping make the roads safer') against NHTSA recall 23V-085 ('increases the risk of a crash'). Does not show: A measured refutation. The README: the recall sentence states no test or measurement, and it concerns FSD Beta in 2023, not today's FSD (Supervised). 'Read it as a regulator pushing back.'
  • #receipts-tests Receipts has an offline test suite that needs no network and no key. Does not show: That the tests pass today. They were not run for this site (the repo was read-only for this build and npm would write to it).
  • #latch-paper I wrote a paper draft reporting the Latch negative result: 'When Gates Abstain Too Often: Typed Operator Gates Fail to Beat Chain-of-Thought on Multi-Hop QA'. Does not show: Submission, review or publication. Status beyond 'draft' is unknown. The worktree has an untracked paper/ directory not read in the walk.
